title: fix(plugin-timeline,plugin-charts,i18n): a stored date-only day reads as that day in every zone on the timeline, a chart's date axis and the i18n date helpers (objectui#10866, slice 2)
body:
Part of #10866
Clause-②: no

Slice 2 of the date-only zone family's carrier card: site 3 (`plugin-timeline`), site 4 (`plugin-charts`) and site 6 (the `@object-ui/i18n` date helpers), per triage `5861646819`, seat 2's release note `5863305580` and claim `5863746430`. Site 5 (core `FormulaFunctions`) is measured, not edited: the measurement and a recommendation are below. The card stays open.

Why `Clause-②: no`: display reads of stored date-only values stop shifting a day west of UTC. No authored key, accepted document or public type moves.

## What changed

Every read below now takes the shared step, `toDisplayDate` from `@object-ui/core` (the objectui#10183 convention). It tells the two shapes apart by the VALUE, never by a declared field type: a date-only `YYYY-MM-DD` string is rebuilt at local midnight of the day it names, and a value with a time part keeps its instant (the engine parse).

- **Site 3, `plugin-timeline`.**
  - `ObjectTimeline`: the date bucket (`startOfDay(toDisplayDate(raw))`) and the sort (a `sortKey` over `toDisplayDate`) now read alike. The vertical renderer groups ADJACENT items, so a sort that disagreed with the buckets ordered "Today" above "Overdue" for a mix of shapes. A value the shared step refuses (unparsable, or a day its month does not have) sorts with the dateless items, where it already bucketed ("No date").
  - The renderer's `formatDate`: the `short` and `long` faces read the local-midnight value. The `iso` face prints a date-only value from local getters (core `toDateInputValue`), because `toISOString()` of a local midnight names the day before east of UTC; an instant keeps its UTC day. A refused value prints as written on `iso`, where `toISOString()` threw `RangeError: Invalid time value` during render.
- **Site 4, `plugin-charts`.** `AdvancedChartImpl`'s `formatTick` reads the category through `toDisplayDate`. Its fallback for a locale `Intl` refuses prints a date-only category from local getters and keeps an instant's UTC day (`isRealCalendarDate` on the category is the split). The span that picks `MMM D` or `MMM YYYY` keeps the engine parse on purpose: it is a duration between two categories, a whole number of days for two UTC midnights, where two local midnights are an hour off across a DST change and a 62-day span would flip faces. A refused category falls through to the raw category.
- **Site 6, the i18n helpers.** `formatDate`, `formatDateTime`, `formatRelativeTime` (`utils/formatting.ts`) and `formatDateSpec` (`utils/spec-formatters.ts`) parse through `toDisplayDate`.
  - `formatDateSpec` applies `timeZone` to an instant only (`isRealCalendarDate` on the string is the split, the same test the shared step makes). A date-only value is formatted in the local zone, the only zone where the shared step's local midnight reads back as its day; `toDisplayDate`'s own contract says to read its result with local getters or local-zone `Intl` only.
  - `formatRelativeTime` returns an unparsable value as its string, the face the other three already give, instead of throwing. It is needed here: the shared step refuses `2026-02-30`, which the engine used to roll.
  - Dependency direction, checked before editing: `@object-ui/i18n` already depends on `@object-ui/core` (it re-exports `number-display` from there) and `core` imports nothing from `i18n`. No cycle, and no copy of the helper.
- **Pins.** Four files registered in `PINS` of `scripts/__tests__/date-only-zone-pins-10183.test.ts` (plus one header sentence): `ObjectTimeline.dateOnlyZone-10866`, `TimelineRenderer.dateOnlyZone-10866`, `AdvancedChartImpl.dateOnlyZone-10866` and `formatting.dateOnlyZone-10866`. Each runs under `America/Los_Angeles` and `Asia/Shanghai`, each zone opens with a rig case and a fixture-validity case, and each carries an instant control. Suite-zone cases run in the normal run too.
- `packages/plugin-timeline/tsconfig.test.json` names `node` types for the pins' `process.env` (TypeScript 6 includes no `@types` by default; `packages/plugin-calendar/tsconfig.test.json` names it for the same pins).
- **Console chunking (fix round 2, contract review `5864479592` item 1; claim amended at `5864501516`).** `apps/console/vite.config.ts`: the `i18n-runtime` manual-chunk group takes `includeDependenciesRecursively: false`. This slice gives `packages/i18n` its first runtime import of `@object-ui/core`, `i18n-runtime` outranks `framework` (83 over 80), and rolldown's default recursive capture followed the import and wrote `framework`'s declared members into `i18n-runtime`, which turned `Bundle Analysis`'s membership half red. The flag is the objectui#9345 repair the config's `data-adapter` paragraph documents; the group's new comment records the circular-chunk re-check that paragraph asks for (readings below). `scripts/__tests__/check-eager-closure-budget.test.ts` pins it: the `data-adapter` options case is now one case per group, `data-adapter` and `i18n-runtime`, each asserting it outranks `framework` and declares the flag. `toDisplayDate` keeps its one home in core; nothing is copied into i18n.
- Docs: one paragraph in `content/docs/plugins/plugin-timeline.mdx` ("Date Formatting") and one in `packages/i18n/README.md` ("Formatting Utilities").
- Changeset `.changeset/10866-timeline-charts-i18n-date-only.md`: `patch` for `@object-ui/plugin-timeline`, `@object-ui/plugin-charts` and `@object-ui/i18n`. Fix round 2 extends its gantt sentence (review item ③a): the variant's axis headers, extent and bar positions are unchanged, so west of UTC its bar tooltip now names the stored day while the axis above it still reads the day before, until a later slice. The console chunking change moves no published file, so it needs no declaration (`check-changeset-presence` counts the same 9 source files of 3 released packages).

## Readings, base `b8e09415c` against head, in both zones

Measured by a throwaway harness on the forks pool with the pins' own fixtures, once over the base sources and once over head (the harness file was deleted; the pins hold the same values).

Timeline, clock `2026-10-06T12:00Z` ("today" is October 6th in both zones), `en-US`:

| reading | LA base | LA head | Shanghai base | Shanghai head |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| feed of `2026-10-06` and `2026-10-07` | Overdue: Ship (10/5/2026) · Today: Review (10/6/2026) | Today: Ship (10/6/2026) · Tomorrow: Review (10/7/2026) | Today: Ship (10/6/2026) · Tomorrow: Review (10/7/2026) | same |
| feed of day `2026-10-06` and instant `2026-10-06T04:00Z` | Overdue: Day (10/5/2026), Instant (10/5/2026) | Overdue: Instant (10/5/2026) · Today: Day (10/6/2026) | Today: Day (10/6/2026), Instant (10/6/2026) | same |
| item `short` / `long`, `2026-10-06` | 10/5/2026 / October 5, 2026 | 10/6/2026 / October 6, 2026 | 10/6/2026 / October 6, 2026 | same |
| item `iso`, `2026-10-06` | 2026-10-06 | 2026-10-06 | 2026-10-06 | 2026-10-06 |
| item `iso`, `2026-02-30` | 2026-03-02 | 2026-02-30 | 2026-03-02 | 2026-02-30 |

Chart x-axis ticks, `en-US`:

| categories | LA base | LA head | Shanghai base | Shanghai head |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `2026-09-01`, `2026-09-02` | Aug 31, Sep 1 | Sep 1, Sep 2 | Sep 1, Sep 2 | Sep 1, Sep 2 |
| `2026-09-01`, `2026-12-01` | Aug 2026, Nov 2026 | Sep 2026, Dec 2026 | Sep 2026, Dec 2026 | same |
| days, refused locale (fallback) | 2026-09-01, 2026-09-02 | same | same | same |
| instants `2026-09-02T03:00Z`, `2026-09-03T03:00Z` | Sep 1, Sep 2 | same | Sep 2, Sep 3 | same |
| instants, refused locale (fallback) | 2026-09-02, 2026-09-03 | same | same | same |
| `2026-02-28`, `2026-02-30` | Feb 27, Mar 1 | Feb 28, 2026-02-30 | Feb 28, Mar 2 | Feb 28, 2026-02-30 |

The two fallback rows are green on base by construction: the old parse was UTC, so its `toISOString()` was right. They are the half a parse-only repair breaks east of UTC; see the second ablation below.

i18n helpers, clock 10:00 on August 30th local in each zone, `en-US`:

| call | LA base | LA head | Shanghai base | Shanghai head |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `formatDate('2026-09-01')` | Aug 31, 2026 | Sep 1, 2026 | Sep 1, 2026 | Sep 1, 2026 |
| `formatDateTime('2026-09-01')` | Aug 31, 2026, 5:00 PM | Sep 1, 2026, 12:00 AM | Sep 1, 2026, 8:00 AM | Sep 1, 2026, 12:00 AM |
| `formatRelativeTime('2026-09-01')` | tomorrow | in 2 days | in 2 days | in 2 days |
| `formatDateSpec('2026-09-01', medium)` | Aug 31, 2026 | Sep 1, 2026 | Sep 1, 2026 | Sep 1, 2026 |
| same with `timeZone: 'America/New_York'` | Aug 31, 2026 | Sep 1, 2026 | Aug 31, 2026 | Sep 1, 2026 |
| `formatDate('2026-09-02T03:00:00.000Z')` (instant) | Sep 1, 2026 | same | Sep 2, 2026 | same |
| `formatDate('2026-02-30')` | Mar 1, 2026 | 2026-02-30 | Mar 2, 2026 | 2026-02-30 |
| `formatRelativeTime('not a date')` | throws RangeError | not a date | throws RangeError | not a date |

The Shanghai `formatDateTime` row moves on the time only (8:00 AM to 12:00 AM): the day was already right there, and a date-only value is now midnight of its day in every zone.

## Site 5, `FormulaFunctions`: measurement only, no edit

Measured with `@objectstack/formula` 17.4.0, the version installed here, and read against objectstack `packages/formula/src/stdlib.ts` and ADR-0053 D1; process zone `America/Los_Angeles` and `Asia/Shanghai`, `now` pinned at `2026-09-28T05:30Z` and `2026-09-28T20:00Z`.

- **Server (CEL stdlib).** There is no `TODAY()` or `DATEADD` by those names; the equivalents are `today()`, `daysFromNow(n)`, `addDays(d, n)`, `addMonths(d, n)` and `daysBetween(a, b)`. A calendar day is a `Date` at UTC midnight of that day (ADR-0053 D1), a date-only string hydrates to UTC midnight, arithmetic runs in UTC, `addMonths` clamps to the month's last day, and `today()` is the calendar day in `EvalContext.timezone` (default UTC) as UTC midnight. No result depends on the process zone. For a CEL default on a `date` field the engine stores such a result as its UTC day (objectql `normalizeExpressionDefault` through `resolveNowDefault`).
  - `today()` at 05:30Z: `2026-09-28T00:00Z` with the zone unset or Shanghai, `2026-09-27T00:00Z` with Los Angeles; at 20:00Z, `2026-09-29T00:00Z` with Shanghai.
  - `addDays('2026-09-01', 1)`: `2026-09-02T00:00Z` everywhere; `addDays('2026-11-01', 1)`: `2026-11-02T00:00Z`; `addMonths('2026-01-31', 1)`: `2026-02-28T00:00Z`.
- **Core `FormulaFunctions`.** `TODAY()` is the UTC day as `YYYY-MM-DD` (`2026-09-28` in both zones at both clocks), so it agrees with the server only while the reference zone is UTC. `DATEADD` parses the UTC midnight, moves it with LOCAL setters and returns an instant string:
  - `DATEADD('2026-09-01', 1, 'day')` gives `2026-09-02T00:00:00.000Z` in both zones (agrees);
  - `DATEADD('2026-11-01', 1, 'day')` in LA gives `2026-11-02T01:00:00.000Z`, and `DATEADD('2026-03-08', 1, 'day')` in LA gives `2026-03-08T23:00:00.000Z` (the server: `2026-11-02` and `2026-03-09` at midnight UTC);
  - `DATEADD('2026-09-01', 1, 'month')` in LA gives `2026-10-02T00:00:00.000Z` (Shanghai and the server: October 1st);
  - `DATEADD('2026-01-31', 1, 'month')` gives `2026-03-03T00:00:00.000Z` in every zone, UTC included (the server clamps to February 28th);
  - `DATEFORMAT('2026-09-01', 'YYYY-MM-DD')` gives `2026-08-31` in LA; `DATEDIFF('2025-12-31', '2026-01-01', 'year')` gives 0 in LA and 1 in Shanghai and UTC.
  - Output shape: a date-only argument comes back as an instant string, which the display path (`toDisplayDate`) then reads as an instant, a day early west of UTC.
- **Recommendation.** The day arithmetic can agree with the server without a new statement, because ADR-0053 D1 already states the model: read a date-only argument at UTC midnight, add days and months with UTC setters (months clamped as `addMonths` does), format with UTC getters, and hand a date-only argument back as `YYYY-MM-DD` (the spec's calendar-day stored form) and an instant as an instant. ONE thing needs a statement, because the server takes it from a context the client does not have: the zone `TODAY()` uses in the browser. Proposed wording for the seat: "ADR-0053's compute-tz axis covers client-evaluated formulas: `TODAY()` in `@object-ui/core` names the calendar day in the same reference timezone the server's `EvalContext.timezone` resolves for that user, and UTC when none is available to the client." Recommended because ADR-0053 puts `today()` on the compute-tz axis (execution context), not the render-tz axis (the viewer), and a client formula that disagrees with the server's saved answer is the worse split; the cost is that `TODAY()` keeps disagreeing with the viewer's own "today" (the timeline's buckets) until that timezone reaches the client.

## Acceptance notes

- **The timeline's gantt-variant axis is not changed** (the card's site-3 line "the axis extent parses then prints `toISOString()`"). `generateTimeScaleHeaders`, `calculateDateRange`, `calculateBarDimensions`, the `findUnusableGanttDate` validity gate and the min-over-max inversion guard still use the engine parse, and `emptyGanttDateRange` (the empty plan's axis) still takes today as the UTC day (`new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]`), not the viewer's. Measured on head: `generateTimeScaleHeaders('day', '2026-10-05', '2026-10-07', 'en-US')` reads Oct 4, Oct 5, Oct 6 in LA (Oct 5, Oct 6, Oct 7 in Shanghai); `'month'` over `2026-10-01` to `2026-12-31` reads Sep 2026, Oct 2026, Nov 2026 in LA. The composed timeline refuses `variant: 'gantt'` (objectui#6655), so only authored rows reach it; `examples/schema-catalog/src/schemas/plugin-timeline/gantt-style-timeline.json` authors date-only rows. Left for a later slice of this card: routing it means the validity gate refuses a day its month does not have and the datetime axis labels move to the viewer's day, two decisions of their own. The bar tooltip on that variant uses `formatDate`, so it now reads the stored day while the headers and bar positions do not: west of UTC a header can read Oct 4 over a bar whose tooltip says 10/5/2026. The changeset says so (fix round 2).
- **Site 6 does have an in-repo caller.** The card says none; `packages/app-shell/src/utils/relativeTime.ts` (`timeAgo`, for notification and activity rows) calls `formatRelativeTime` with epoch milliseconds from an instant, which never takes the date-only arm. Its behaviour does not move.
- `formatRelativeTime` still counts from now to an instant, now local midnight for a date-only value: at 01:00 on August 31st, `2026-09-01` reads "in 23 hours" (derived, not measured), which is what a UTC viewer always read at 01:00 UTC. Calendar-day phrasing is a separate decision.
- `formatDateSpec` with a `timeStyle` and a date-only value prints midnight in the viewer's zone (and, for `long` or `full`, that zone's name).
- Remaining engine parses in the touched packages, each deliberate: the chart span (a duration, above); the "now" clocks; the gantt-axis reads (above).
